H.Â L. Mencken's Happy Days describes how his father, the owner of a factory that produced these items, broke a strike by hiring tramps. A man from this non-Jamaica colony kept a repetitive, coded diary that details his "rogering" of various women and the whippings he gave his slaves. During the Battle of Beroia, members of this military organization hacked through a wagon fort, resulting in a decisive defeat for the Pechenegs. Name this mother of Joseph II, a Habsburg queen whose succession was allowed by the Pragmatic Sanction.

A ruler of this dynasty was advised by the Jew Yaqub ibn Killis and, according to legend, converted to Christianity after watching Simon the Tanner lift a mountain into the air. After Daniel Conover obtained an arrest warrant for this city's mayor, its Municipal and Metropolitan police forces clashed in an 1857 battle. This city's Roach Guards, nicknamed for their symbol of a dead rabbit, sparked unrest in this city during the tenure of mayor Fernando Wood by attacking the Bowery Boys gang in the Five Points neighborhood. Members of this group guarded wills and testaments and could pardon condemned criminals if they coincidentally met in the street. To indicate the start date of a certain event, runners traveled between these places distributing knotted yucca ropes.
